main.description: How you like Rainshare to work for you. Unlike your profile, this isn't about you for other people to read, but like every record in your repo it is public.

github.description: Your GitHub username, if you've given it. Apps use it to open your fork of an ask's repository in Claude Code on the web or the Claude app, where the agent can push, and to spot the pull requests you open that mention an ask. It isn't checked against GitHub: it only steers what you're shown.

notify.description: The direct messages you'd like from Rainshare's Bluesky account, @rainshare.dev, only ever when there's news: updates within a minute or two, and new asks once a day. Left out, none. Replying STOP to one stops them, whatever this says.

updates.description: News about your asks and what you've helped with: someone's on one, work's been turned in, or it's been marked done or closed.

newAsks.description: How many new asks there are on the board, once a day: the ones projects, ideas and from say.

projects.description: Whether the new asks counted include projects: asks with a repo or an issue to work in. Left out, they do.

ideas.description: Whether the new asks counted include ideas: asks with no repo yet. Left out, they don't.

from.description: Whose new asks are counted, by how you know whoever asked. mutuals: you follow each other. following: you follow them. followers: they follow you. A follow on Bluesky or on Tangled counts. vouched: you, or someone you vouched for, vouched for them on Tangled, and nobody there denounced them. Left out, anyone's.

send.description: What "Direct my agent" does: how the ask is handed to your agent, whether it tells whoever asked that you're on it, and for how long.

route.description: brief: copy the brief, to paste into any agent. web: open Claude Code on the web (the Claude app, on a phone) with the brief and the repository filled in, on a GitHub repository. claude, cloud, codex: copy a command that clones the repo and starts Claude Code (locally or as a cloud session) or Codex with the brief. cli: the Rainshare CLI's run command. mcp: add Rainshare's MCP server to your agent. Apps fall back to the brief when a route doesn't suit an ask.

claim.description: Whether directing your agent also says you're on it (writes a dev.rainshare.take). Left out, it does.

days.description: How many days you usually give yourself to turn the work in: the until on the takes you write.

askEachTime.description: Whether to ask these questions each time you direct your agent, with these answers picked. Left out, apps ask.

terms.description: That you agreed to Rainshare's Terms of Service: which version, and when. Written when you agree, on the site or with the CLI. Rainshare keeps a note of its own as well, checked against this record.

version.description: The version agreed to: the date the terms last changed in a way people are asked to agree to again, as YYYY-MM-DD.
